scripts.verify: npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:coverage && npm run build && npm run size && npm run deleted && npm run check:tailwind

//axe-core: `axe-core` was already in the tree as a transitive of `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`, and is declared as a direct devDependency because `src/a11y.browser.test.tsx` imports it. An engine whose exact findings a test's expectations are pinned to should not have its version chosen by a lint plugin's resolution: a jsx-a11y bump could move axe a minor, change what the sweep reports, and leave nothing in either file to say why. Dev-only -- nothing outside that test imports it, so it reaches no bundle and the size budget does not move.
//overrides: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@6.10.2 -- the latest published -- declares `eslint@^3 || … || ^9`, and this project is on eslint@10. There is no version of the plugin that accepts 10; `npm view` shows 6.10.2 as `latest` with no prerelease. So the choice was: drop the plugin from phase 0, install the whole tree with `--legacy-peer-deps` (which silences *every* peer conflict in the repository, including the next real one), or narrow the exception to the single package that needs it. This is the third. It pins the plugin's `eslint` to the root's rather than letting npm hunt for a second copy, which is also what we want on the merits: two eslint versions in one tree is its own bug. The cost is that the plugin now runs outside its author's declared support window, so a break would be ours to notice -- which is why the plugin is exercised by `npm run lint` over the whole of `src/` in this very commit, and why `eslint.config.test.ts` asserts the rules actually fire rather than merely that the config loads. Remove this override the moment the plugin declares eslint 10.
